# Module for creating interactive plots
import plotly.graph_objs as graph

# Creating a Candlestick chart for Berkshire Hathaway stocks
candlestick = graph.Candlestick(
    # Setting the x-axis to the dates from the DataFrame index
    x=data.index,
    # Setting the opening prices
    open=data['Open'],
    # Setting the high price
    high=data['High'],
    # Setting the low price
    low=data['Low'],
    # Setting the adjusted closing price
    close=data['Adj Close'],
    
    increasing=dict(line=dict(color='yellow')),  # Changed the color for increasing price to yellow
    decreasing=dict(line=dict(color='red')),    # Changed the color for decreasing price as red
    
    showlegend=False
)

# Layout configuration
layout = graph.Layout(
    title='Berkshire Hathaway Shares Price - 2016 to 2024',  # Updated the title to reflect the correct date range
    yaxis=dict(title='Price'), # Setting the y-axis title
    xaxis=dict(title='Date'), # Setting the x-axis title
    template='plotly_dark',  # Changed the template to 'plotly_dark' for a different visual style
    xaxis_rangeslider_visible=False,
    margin=dict(t=50, l=50, r=50, b=50)
)

fig = graph.Figure(data=[candlestick], layout=layout)

# Adding annotation to the plot
fig.add_annotation(
    text='Berkshire Hathaway', 
    font=dict(color='white', size=20),  # Changed font color to white and adjusted size
    xref='paper', yref='paper',
    x=0.5, y=0.95,  # Moved annotation closer to the top
    showarrow=False,
    opacity=0.85
)

# Display figure
fig.show()

import optuna
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, r2_score

# Standardize features outside the function
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)

# Objective function for Optuna to tune Linear Regression
def objective(trial):
    # Hyperparameters to tune
    fit_intercept = trial.suggest_categorical('fit_intercept', [True, False])
    normalize = trial.suggest_categorical('normalize', [True, False])
    
    # Create LinearRegression model with the suggested parameters
    model = LinearRegression(fit_intercept=fit_intercept, normalize=normalize)
    
    # Fit the model on the training data
    model.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # Make predictions on the test data
    y_pred = model.predict(X_test_scaled)
    
    # Evaluate model performance
    r2 = r2_score(y_test, y_pred)
    
    # Optuna will maximize the R2 score
    return r2

# Create an Optuna study and optimize the objective function
study = optuna.create_study(direction='maximize')
study.optimize(objective, n_trials=100)  # Run 100 trials to find the best hyperparameters

# Print the best hyperparameters and R2 score
print("Best parameters:", study.best_params)
print("Best R2 score:", study.best_value)

# Train the final model with the best parameters
best_params = study.best_params
final_model = LinearRegression(
    fit_intercept=best_params['fit_intercept'],
    normalize=best_params['normalize']
)

# Fit final model on scaled data
final_model.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)

# Make predictions
y_pred_final = final_model.predict(X_test_scaled)

# Evaluate final model performance
print('Mean Absolute Error:', metrics.mean_absolute_error(y_test, y_pred_final))  
print('Root Mean Squared Error:', np.sqrt(metrics.mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred_final)))
print('R2: ', metrics.r2_score(y_test, y_pred_final))

from sklearn.linear_model import Lasso
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score, mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, explained_variance_score
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import optuna
import numpy as np

# Scale the features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)

# Define the objective function for Optuna
def objective(trial):
    # Suggest a value for alpha on a logarithmic scale
    #alpha = trial.suggest_loguniform('alpha', 1e-10, 1e3)
    
    # Suggest additional hyperparameters for the Lasso model
    max_iter = trial.suggest_int('max_iter', 1000, 50000, step=1000)
    tol = trial.suggest_loguniform('tol', 1e-10, 1e-2)
    fit_intercept = trial.suggest_categorical('fit_intercept', [True, False])
    normalize = trial.suggest_categorical('normalize', [True, False])
    selection = trial.suggest_categorical('selection', ['cyclic', 'random'])
    
    # Initialize Lasso model with the suggested hyperparameters
    model = Lasso(
       # alpha=alpha, 
        max_iter=max_iter, 
        tol=tol, 
        fit_intercept=fit_intercept, 
        normalize=normalize, 
        selection=selection, 
        random_state=42
    )
    
    # Fit the model on training data
    model.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
    
    # Predict on the test set
    b_pred = model.predict(X_test_scaled)
    
    # Calculate the R2 score
    r2 = r2_score(y_test, b_pred)
    
    # Optuna will maximize the objective, so return R2
    return r2

# Set up the Optuna study
study = optuna.create_study(direction='maximize')
study.optimize(objective, n_trials=200)  # Increase n_trials for a more exhaustive search

# Print the best alpha and R2 score
print("Best parameters:", study.best_params)
print("Best R2 score:", study.best_value)

# Train final model with best parameters
best_params = study.best_params
best_lasso_model = Lasso(
    #alpha=best_params['alpha'], 
    max_iter=best_params['max_iter'], 
    tol=best_params['tol'], 
    fit_intercept=best_params['fit_intercept'], 
    normalize=best_params['normalize'], 
    selection=best_params['selection'],
    random_state=42
)
best_lasso_model.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
y_pred_tunned_lasso = best_lasso_model.predict(X_test_scaled)

# Plot predictions vs actual for the tuned model
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
plt.title('Lasso Regression (Tuned with Optuna) | Price vs Time')
plt.plot(X_test_scaled, y_pred_tunned_lasso, color='r', label='Tuned Predicted Price')
plt.scatter(X_test_scaled, y_test, edgecolor='w', label='Actual Price')
plt.xlabel('Integer Date')
plt.ylabel('Stock Price in $')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

# Calculate and print values of MAE, MSE, RMSE
print('Mean Absolute Error:', mean_absolute_error(y_test, y_pred_tunned_lasso))    
print('Root Mean Squared Error:', np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred_tunned_lasso)))
print('R2: ', r2_score(y_test, y_pred_tunned_lasso))

from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import PolynomialFeatures, StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, r2_score
import optuna
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Define the objective function for Optuna
def objective(trial):
    # Suggest a value for alpha on a logarithmic scale
    alpha = trial.suggest_loguniform('alpha', 1e-4, 1e4)
    
    # Suggest values for additional Ridge parameters
    max_iter = trial.suggest_int('max_iter', 1000, 20000, step=500)
    tol = trial.suggest_loguniform('tol', 1e-6, 1e-2)
    fit_intercept = trial.suggest_categorical('fit_intercept', [True, False])
    solver = trial.suggest_categorical('solver', ['auto', 'svd', 'cholesky', 'sparse_cg', 'sag', 'saga'])
    
    # Optionally add Polynomial features
    add_poly_features = trial.suggest_categorical('add_poly_features', [True, False])
    if add_poly_features:
        poly_degree = trial.suggest_int('poly_degree', 2, 5)  # degree for polynomial features
        poly = PolynomialFeatures(degree=poly_degree, include_bias=False)
        X_train_scaled_poly = poly.fit_transform(X_train_scaled)
        X_test_scaled_poly = poly.transform(X_test_scaled)
    else:
        X_train_scaled_poly = X_train_scaled
        X_test_scaled_poly = X_test_scaled

    # Initialize Ridge model with the suggested parameters
    model = Ridge(
        alpha=alpha,
        max_iter=max_iter,
        tol=tol,
        fit_intercept=fit_intercept,
        solver=solver
    )
    
    # Use cross-validation to evaluate the model
    score = cross_val_score(model, X_train_scaled_poly, y_train, cv=5, scoring='r2').mean()
    
    return score

# Scale the data
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)

# Create a study to optimize the model
study = optuna.create_study(direction='maximize')
study.optimize(objective, n_trials=100)

# Print the best parameters and model score
print(f"Best parameters: {study.best_params}")
print(f"Best R2 score: {study.best_value}")

# Train final model with best parameters
best_params = study.best_params
best_ridge_model = Ridge(
    alpha=best_params['alpha'],
    max_iter=best_params['max_iter'],
    tol=best_params['tol'],
    fit_intercept=best_params['fit_intercept'],
    solver=best_params['solver']
)

# If polynomial features were used, transform the data
if best_params['add_poly_features']:
    poly = PolynomialFeatures(degree=best_params['poly_degree'], include_bias=False)
    X_train_scaled_poly = poly.fit_transform(X_train_scaled)
    X_test_scaled_poly = poly.transform(X_test_scaled)
else:
    X_train_scaled_poly = X_train_scaled
    X_test_scaled_poly = X_test_scaled

# Fit the best model on training data
best_ridge_model.fit(X_train_scaled_poly, y_train)

# Make predictions on the test set
y_pred_tunned_ridge = best_ridge_model.predict(X_test_scaled_poly)

# Plot the sorted values for the test set
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
plt.title(f'Ridge Regression (Tuned with Optuna) | Price vs Time')

# Sort values for a smooth line plot
sorted_indices_test = np.argsort(X_test.flatten())
X_test_sorted = X_test[sorted_indices_test]
y_test_sorted = y_test.iloc[sorted_indices_test]
y_pred_tunned_ridge_sorted = y_pred_tunned_ridge[sorted_indices_test]
r2=r2_score(y_test, y_pred_tunned_ridge)
# Plot the actual prices as a line graph
plt.plot(X_test_sorted, y_test_sorted, label='Actual Price', color='blue', linestyle='-', marker='o', markersize=4)

# Plot the tuned predicted prices as a line graph
plt.plot(X_test_sorted, y_pred_tunned_ridge_sorted, label='Tuned Predicted Price', color='red', linestyle='-', marker='x', markersize=4)

# Adding labels and legend
plt.xlabel('Integer Date')
plt.ylabel('Stock Price in $')
box = dict(boxstyle="round, pad=0.3", fc="white", ec="gray", lw=1)
plt.text(plt.xlim()[1], plt.ylim()[1] - 250, f"R²: {r2:.2f}", ha='right', va='top', wrap=True, bbox=box, fontsize=18)
plt.legend()

# Display the graph
plt.show()

# Calculate and print values of MAE, MSE, RMSE, R2
print('Mean Absolute Error:', mean_absolute_error(y_test, y_pred_tunned_ridge))  
print('Root Mean Squared Error:', np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred_tunned_ridge)))
print('R2: ', r2_score(y_test, y_pred_tunned_ridge))

from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
# Define the objective function for Optuna
def objective(trial):
    # Suggest a degree for the polynomial features
    degree = trial.suggest_int('degree', 1, 20)  # You can adjust the range based on your needs
    
    # Initialize polynomial features and linear regression within a pipeline
    model = make_pipeline(
        PolynomialFeatures(degree=degree, include_bias=False),
        StandardScaler(),
        LinearRegression()
    )
    
    # Fit the model on training data
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    
    # Predict on the test set
    y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
    
    # Calculate the R2 score
    r2 = r2_score(y_test, y_pred)
    
    # Optuna will maximize the objective, so return R2
    return r2

# Set up the Optuna study
study = optuna.create_study(direction='maximize')
study.optimize(objective, n_trials=50)  # Increase n_trials for a more exhaustive search

# Print the best degree and R2 score
print("Best degree parameter:", study.best_params['degree'])
print("Best R2 score:", study.best_value)

# Train final model with best degree
best_degree = study.best_params['degree']
best_model = make_pipeline(
    PolynomialFeatures(degree=best_degree, include_bias=False),
    StandardScaler(),
    LinearRegression()
)
best_model.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred_tunned_poly = best_model.predict(X_test)

# Sort values for a smooth plot in the test set
sorted_indices_test = np.argsort(X_test.flatten())
X_test_sorted = X_test[sorted_indices_test]
y_test_sorted = y_test.iloc[sorted_indices_test]
X_test_poly_sorted = X_test_poly[sorted_indices_test]

# Plot the sorted values for the test set
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
plt.title(f'Polynomial Regression (Degree={best_degree} | Tuned with Optuna) | Price vs Time')
plt.scatter(X_test_sorted, y_test_sorted, edgecolor='w', label='Actual Price')
plt.plot(X_test_sorted, y_pred_tunned_poly[sorted_indices_test], color='r', label='Tuned Predicted Price')
plt.xlabel('Integer Date')
plt.ylabel('Stock Price in $')
plt.legend()
plt.show()


# Calculate and print values of MAE, MSE, RMSE
print('Mean Absolute Error:', metrics.mean_absolute_error(y_test, y_pred_tunned_poly))  
print('Root Mean Squared Error:', np.sqrt(metrics.mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred_tunned_poly)))
print('R2: ', metrics.r2_score(y_test, y_pred_tunned_poly))

plt.text(plt.xlim()[1], plt.ylim()[1] - 250, f"R²: {r2_t}", ha='right', va='top', wrap=True, bbox=box, fontsize=18)
plt.legend()
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()

# Show plot
plt.show()

# Ensure Date is datetime type and sort data by date
df['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Date'])
df = df.sort_values('Date').set_index('Date')

# --- Trading Strategy based on Predictions ---

# Calculate signals based on Prediction
df['Signal'] = 0  # Default to no action
df['Signal'][1:] = [1 if df['Prediction'].iloc[i] > df['Close'].iloc[i-1] else -1 for i in range(1, len(df))]

# Initialize variables for trading strategy
initial_balance = 10000  # Starting with $10,000
balance = initial_balance
holdings = 0
trade_log = []
annual_trading_results = {}

# Execute trades based on signals
for i in range(1, len(df)):
    price = df['Close'].iloc[i]
    signal = df['Signal'].iloc[i]

    if signal == 1 and balance >= price:  # Buy
        quantity = balance // price  # Buying as many shares as possible
        balance -= quantity * price
        holdings += quantity
        trade_log.append((df.index[i], 'Buy', quantity, price))
    elif signal == -1 and holdings > 0:  # Sell
        balance += holdings * price
        trade_log.append((df.index[i], 'Sell', holdings, price))
        holdings = 0

    # At the end of each year, record the balance for annual profit calculation
    if i == len(df) - 1 or df.index[i].year != df.index[i + 1].year:
        year = df.index[i].year
        year_end_balance = balance + holdings * price
        annual_profit = year_end_balance - initial_balance  # Profit in dollars
        annual_profit_percentage = (annual_profit / initial_balance) * 100  # Profit in percentage
        if year >= 2016:  # Include only results from 2018 onward
            annual_trading_results[year] = {
                'Balance': year_end_balance,
                'Profit': annual_profit,
                'Profit_Percentage': annual_profit_percentage
            }
        # Reset initial balance to track annual returns
        initial_balance = year_end_balance

# Calculate final balance for trading strategy
final_balance_trading = balance + holdings * df['Close'].iloc[-1]  # Convert holdings to cash
profit_trading = final_balance_trading - initial_balance

# --- Buy and Hold Strategy (Annual) ---

buy_and_hold_results = {}
for year in range(2016, 2024):  # Only calculate from 2018 to 2023
    try:
        # Buy at the beginning of the year
        buy_price = df['Close'][df.index.year == year].iloc[0]
        # Sell at the end of the year
        sell_price = df['Close'][df.index.year == year].iloc[-1]
        # Calculate annual return
        annual_return = ((sell_price - buy_price) / buy_price) * 100  # in percentage
        buy_and_hold_results[year] = annual_return
    except IndexError:
        continue


# --- Output Results for Comparison ---

print("\nTrading Strategy Results (Annual):")
for year, result in annual_trading_results.items():
    print(f"Year: {year}, Balance: ${result['Balance']:.2f}, Profit: ${result['Profit']:.2f}, Profit Percentage: {result['Profit_Percentage']:.2f}%")

# Calculate Cumulative Return for Trading Strategy
annual_profits = [result['Profit_Percentage'] for result in annual_trading_results.values()]
cumulative_growth_trading = 1
for profit in annual_profits:
    cumulative_growth_trading *= (1 + profit / 100)
cumulative_return_trading = (cumulative_growth_trading - 1) * 100
print(f"Cumulative Return for Trading Strategy: {cumulative_return_trading:.2f}%")

print("\nBuy and Hold Strategy Results (Annual):")
for year, annual_return in buy_and_hold_results.items():
    print(f"Year: {year}, Annual Return: {annual_return:.2f}%")

# Calculate Cumulative Return for Buy and Hold Strategy
annual_returns = list(buy_and_hold_results.values())
cumulative_growth_bh = 1
for r in annual_returns:
    cumulative_growth_bh *= (1 + r / 100)
cumulative_return_bh = (cumulative_growth_bh - 1) * 100
print(f"Cumulative Return for Buy and Hold Strategy: {cumulative_return_bh:.2f}%")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np



# Data for Trading Strategy
trading_years = [2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023]
trading_profits = [23.04, 26.00, 17.80, 20.61, 33.72, 28.95, 25.07, 14.74]
trading_cumulative = 445.04

# Data for Buy and Hold Strategy
buy_and_hold_profits = [24.65, 20.99, 3.53, 11.69, 1.52, 30.88, 2.70, 15.09]
buy_and_hold_cumulative = 173.86

# Create bar width
bar_width = 0.35
x = np.arange(len(trading_years))

# Plot annual returns comparison
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 7))
plt.bar(x - bar_width/2, trading_profits, width=bar_width, label='Trading Strategy', color='blue')
plt.bar(x + bar_width/2, buy_and_hold_profits, width=bar_width, label='Buy and Hold Strategy', color='orange')
plt.xticks(x, trading_years ,fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel('Year', fontsize=16)
plt.ylabel('Annual Return (%)', fontsize=16)
plt.title('Annual Returns Comparison: Trading vs Buy and Hold', fontsize=16)
plt.legend(fontsize=14)
plt.show()

# Plot cumulative returns comparison
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
strategies = ['Trading Strategy', 'Buy and Hold']
cumulative_returns = [trading_cumulative, buy_and_hold_cumulative]
bar = plt.bar(strategies, cumulative_returns, color=['blue', 'orange'])

# Add cumulative return values on top of the bars
for bar, value in zip(bar, cumulative_returns):
    plt.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 5, f'{value:.2f}%', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10)
    
plt.ylabel('Cumulative Return (%)')
plt.title('Cumulative Returns Comparison: Trading vs Buy and Hold', pad=8)
plt.show()
